```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
#| cache: false
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)
theme_set(theme_grey(base_size = 16))
options(scipen = 0)
```

## General approach

![](img/day3/statistics_approach.png){width="70%"}

:::{.aside}

Please note the discussion about p-values as a basis for binary decisions.
  See e.g. [here](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41592-019-0470-3) or [here](https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-019-00857-9) as a starting point

:::

## Tests to compare two groups

```{r}
#| include: false
schematic <- tibble(
  group = rep(c("Group 1", "Group 2"), each = 6),
  value = c(2.1, 2.9, 3.4, 3.8, 4.5, 5.0, 3.6, 4.3, 4.8, 5.3, 5.9, 6.6)
) |>
  mutate(rank = rank(value))
schematic_means <- summarize(schematic, value = mean(value), .by = group)
schematic_sums <- summarize(schematic, rank_sum = sum(rank), .by = group) |>
  mutate(
    label = paste(group, "rank sum:", rank_sum),
    x = c(3.5, 9.5)
  )
```

:::{.columns}

:::{.column width="50%"}

:::{.fragment}

**t-test**

:::

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 4.5
#| fig-height: 2.4
ggplot(schematic, aes(x = group, y = value, color = group)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  geom_crossbar(
    data = schematic_means,
    aes(ymin = value, ymax = value),
    width = 0.4
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("cyan4", "darkorange")) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    axis.title = element_blank(),
    axis.text.y = element_blank()
  )
```

:::{.fragment}

:::{.nonincremental}

- Compares the **means** of two groups
- Suitable for roughly normal data, or for larger samples
- 2 versions: Student's (equal variance) and Welch's t-test
  - Welch's t-test is a good default

:::

:::

:::

:::{.column width="50%"}

:::{.fragment}

**Wilcoxon rank-sum test**

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 4.5
#| fig-height: 2.4
ggplot(schematic, aes(x = rank, y = 1, color = group)) +
  geom_text(aes(label = rank), size = 7, fontface = "bold") +
  geom_text(
    data = schematic_sums,
    aes(x = x, y = 0.4, label = label),
    size = 5
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("cyan4", "darkorange")) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0.2, 1.3)) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

:::{.nonincremental}

- Compares **ranks**: does one group tend to have larger values?
- Useful for ordinal data, skewed small samples, or outliers

:::

:::

:::

:::

## The data: iris

**Question:** Does the sepal width differ between *I. versicolor* and *I. virginica*?

:::{.columns}

:::{.column width="50%"}

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Reproduce the data"
flowers <- as_tibble(iris) |>
  filter(Species %in% c("versicolor", "virginica")) |>
  select(sepal_width = Sepal.Width, species = Species) |>
  droplevels()
```

```{r}
flowers
```

:::

:::{.column width="50%"}

![Image from [medium.com](https://medium.com/data-science/k-medoids-clustering-on-iris-data-set-1931bf781e05)](img/day3/iris.png)

Sepal width (in cm) of 50 flowers from each of two iris species

:::

:::



## First look at the data

:::{.columns}

:::{.column width="50%"}

```{r}
flowers |>
  summarize(
    n = n(),
    mean = mean(sepal_width),
    sd = sd(sepal_width),
    .by = species
  )
```

:::

:::{.column width="50%"}

```{r}
#| fig-height: 5.5
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Code for the boxplot"
ggplot(flowers, aes(x = species, y = sepal_width)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  geom_point(
    position = position_jitter(width = 0.08, height = 0, seed = 123),
    alpha = 0.6
  ) +
  labs(x = "Species", y = "Sepal width (cm)")
```

:::

:::

## Prepare the group vectors

Most test functions take the values of each group as a vector

```{r}
versicolor <- filter(flowers, species == "versicolor")$sepal_width
virginica <- filter(flowers, species == "virginica")$sepal_width
```

. . .

<br>
```{r}
versicolor
```

## Shapiro-Wilk test for normality

. . .

$H_0$: The data come from a normal distribution

```{r}
shapiro.test(versicolor)
shapiro.test(virginica)
```

- A **large p-value**: no evidence against normality, can not reject $H_0$
- With large samples, very small deviations can give small p-values
- Always look at the data as well

## Normality with QQ-plots

Points should roughly follow the line. Look at the **tails** and at **unusual observations**.


## Compare two means: Welch's t-test

$H_0$: The means of the two groups do not differ



```{r}
t.test(versicolor, virginica)
```

- t: test statistic (t = 0 if the means are equal)
- p-value: How likely is a difference at least this large if the means were equal?
- Reject $H_0$

. . .

Mean sepal width was **0.20 cm smaller** in *I. versicolor* than in *I. virginica* (Welch's t-test, $t_{97.9}$ = -3.21, p = 0.002).

## Wilcoxon rank-sum test

$H_0$: Neither group tends to have larger values than the other

- All values are ranked from smallest to largest
- The test compares the ranks of the two groups
- **Demonstration only:** the iris data don't need a rank-based test, t-test was fine here

. . .

```{r}
wilcox.test(versicolor, virginica)
```

. . .

Sepal width tended to be smaller in *I. versicolor* than in *I. virginica* (Wilcoxon rank-sum test, W = 841, p = 0.005).

## Paired observations

Examples of paired observations:

:::{.nonincremental}

- Blood pressure of patients before and after medication
- Difference in sleep quality of people as children and adults
- Biodiversity in rivers before and after a power plant
...

:::

. . .

In `sleep`, the **same 10 people** received two drugs (`extra`: extra sleep in hours)

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Reproduce the data"
sleep_paired <- sleep |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = group,
    names_prefix = "drug_",
    values_from = extra
  )
```

```{r}
sleep_paired
```

## Paired observations

```{r}
#| flourish:
#|   - target: "paired = TRUE"
t.test(
  sleep_paired$drug_1,
  sleep_paired$drug_2,
  paired = TRUE
)
```

Also: `wilcox.test(..., paired = TRUE)`

. . .

People slept **1.58 h longer** with drug 2 than with drug 1 (paired t-test, $t_9$ = -4.06, p = 0.003).

# Visualizing test results {.inverse}

## Boxplot to show differences

```{r}
#| output-location: column
#| fig-height: 5.5
ggplot(
  flowers,
  aes(x = species, y = sepal_width)
) +
  geom_boxplot()
```

## Add a test with `geom_signif()`

The [`ggsignif`](https://const-ae.github.io/ggsignif/) package adds significance levels to a ggplot

```{r}
#| output-location: column
#| fig-height: 5.5
# install.packages("ggsignif")
library(ggsignif)

ggplot(
  flowers,
  aes(x = species, y = sepal_width)
) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  geom_signif(
    comparisons = list(
      c("versicolor", "virginica")
    ),
    test = "t.test",
    map_signif_level = TRUE
  )
```

:::{.nonincremental}

- `test = "t.test"`: Welch's t-test (the default is a Wilcoxon test)
- `map_signif_level = TRUE`: stars, `FALSE`: p-value

:::

## Plot means with `stat_summary()`

```{r}
#| output-location: column
#| fig-height: 5.5
#| flourish:
#|   - target: "stat_summary()"
ggplot(
  flowers,
  aes(x = species, y = sepal_width)
) +
  stat_summary()
```

:::{.nonincremental}

- By default, `stat_summary()` shows the mean ± standard error (SE)

:::

## Style means and error bars

```{r}
#| output-location: column
#| fig-height: 5.5
ggplot(
  flowers,
  aes(x = species, y = sepal_width)
) +
  stat_summary(
    fun.data = mean_se,
    geom = "errorbar",
    width = 0.15
  ) +
  stat_summary(
    fun = mean,
    geom = "point",
    color = "#28a87d",
    size = 4
  )
```

:::{.nonincremental}

- `fun.data` for error bars, `fun` for points

:::

# Comparing three groups {.inverse}

## Actually, there were three species

**Question:** Does the sepal width differ between the three iris species?

:::{.columns}

:::{.column width="50%"}

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Reproduce the data"
flowers_all <- as_tibble(iris) |>
  select(sepal_width = Sepal.Width, species = Species)
```

```{r}
flowers_all |>
  summarize(
    n = n(),
    mean = mean(sepal_width),
    .by = species
  )
```

:::

:::{.column width="50%"}

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-height: 5.5
ggplot(flowers_all, aes(x = species, y = sepal_width)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  geom_point(
    position = position_jitter(width = 0.08, height = 0, seed = 123),
    alpha = 0.6
  ) +
  labs(x = "Species", y = "Sepal width (cm)")
```

:::

:::

. . . 

Could we just run 3 separate t-tests?

## Two kinds of errors

Every test decision can be wrong in two ways:

| | $H_0$ is true (no difference) | $H_0$ is false (real difference) |
|---|---|---|
| **Reject $H_0$** | **Type I error**: false positive (probability α) | Correct |
| **Do not reject $H_0$** | Correct | **Type II error**: false negative |

. . .

- With α = 0.05, we accept a 5% risk of a false positive
- Multiple testing increases the risk of a **type I error**

## Error-inflation with multiple testing

- For one test: Chance of false positive is 5% (at α = 0.05)
- This error potential increases with multiple tests:

. . .

$$P(\text{at least one false positive}) = 1 - (1 - \alpha)^k$$

with $k$ = number of tests

. . .

| Number of tests | Chance of at least one false positive |
|---:|---:|
| 1 | 5% |
| 3 | 14.3% |
| 10 | 40.1% |

. . .

Solution: p-value correction for multiple testing

## Pairwise comparisons in R

```{r}
pairwise.t.test(
  flowers_all$sepal_width,
  flowers_all$species,
  pool.sd = FALSE
)
```

:::{.nonincremental}

- `pool.sd = FALSE`: Welch's t-test for each pair (the default uses one shared SD across all groups)
- The p-values are already adjusted (Holm method is the default)
- Rank-based alternative: `pairwise.wilcox.test()`

:::

## Add the adjusted p-values to a plot

`geom_signif` can't run pairwise tests, so we need to add p-values manually.

```{r}
#| output-location: column
#| fig-height: 5.5
#| flourish:
#|   - target: "annotations = c"
#|   - target: "step_increase = 0.1,"
ggplot(
  flowers_all,
  aes(x = species, y = sepal_width)
) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  geom_signif(
    comparisons = list(
      c("setosa", "versicolor"),
      c("setosa", "virginica"),
      c("versicolor", "virginica")
    ),
    annotations = c(
      "p = 7.5e-15",
      "p = 9.1e-09",
      "p = 0.0018"
    ),
    step_increase = 0.1,
    tip_length = 0.02
  )
```

:::{.nonincremental}

- `annotations`: show our adjusted p-values (no new tests)
- `step_increase`: stack the brackets

:::

## Extract the p-values automatically

Typing p-values by hand is error-prone. Extract them with `p["row", "column"]`:

:::{.columns}

:::{.column width="50%"}

```{r}
pairwise_results <- pairwise.t.test(
  flowers_all$sepal_width,
  flowers_all$species,
  pool.sd = FALSE
)
p <- pairwise_results$p.value

comparisons <- list(
  c("setosa", "versicolor"),
  c("setosa", "virginica"),
  c("versicolor", "virginica")
)
adjusted_p <- c(
  p["versicolor", "setosa"],
  p["virginica", "setosa"],
  p["virginica", "versicolor"]
)
p_labels <- paste(
  "p =",
  format.pval(adjusted_p, digits = 2)
)
```

:::

:::{.column width="50%"}

```{r}
#| eval: false
ggplot(
  flowers_all,
  aes(x = species, y = sepal_width)
) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  geom_signif(
    comparisons = comparisons,
    annotations = p_labels,
    step_increase = 0.1,
    tip_length = 0.02
  )
```

:::

:::
